# Figures {.figure-page-title}

The 910 occupations of the paper, on the six axes recovered from O\*NET.
The coordinates are in [`output/occupation_coordinates.csv`](output/occupation_coordinates.csv), one row
per occupation.

## The occupation space {#space}

```{=html}
<figure class="plot-figure">
  <div class="plot-pickers">
    <fieldset class="plot-controls plot-picker" id="space-picker">
      <legend>Axes (tick one to three)</legend>

    <fieldset class="plot-controls plot-picker plot-picker-small" id="colour-picker">
      <legend>Colour (optional)</legend>
    </fieldset>
  </div>
  <div class="plot plot-space" id="plot-space" role="img"
       aria-label="Scatter plot of 910 occupations on one to three of the six axes, chosen with the boxes above, and optionally coloured by one axis. By default R1, R2 and R3, coloured by R4."></div>
  <figcaption>Figure 5.8: the six-axis space. Three ticked axes span
  the space, two a plane and one a line, whose vertical spread only separates
  the points; ticked axes are taken in order from R1 to R6. Any one axis can
  be chosen as the colour, or none. Dotted lines in the plane and the line mark
  the medians. Each axis is named by its + pole and its − pole. Drag to rotate;
  hold ⌘ or Ctrl and scroll to zoom; hover for the occupation.</figcaption>
</figure>
```
